title: Short Stuff: James Dean's Car
summary: Short Stuff episode on James Dean's 1955 Porsche 550 Spyder, nicknamed "Little Bastard." Covers the crash at the Route 46 and 41 intersection near Cholame/Salinas that killed Dean, the car's afterlife: salvage, William Eschrich and Troy Lee McHenry crashes and the "cursed" idea, George Barris's claims about the frame and a display that fell and killed a truck driver, a reported storage fire, a 2015 Volo Auto Museum hidden-car tip (building demolished), and a transaxle sold at auction for about $400,000. Closes with a tangent about the hosts' Smokey and the Bandit sheriff's car door.

segments.title: James Dean's fatal crash
segments.summary: Hosts introduce James Dean's Porsche 550 Spyder and describe the 1955 crash at the intersection of Routes 46 and 41, where Donald Turnupseed turned in front of Dean. Dean's mechanic Rolf Wutherich was thrown clear; Dean died of a broken neck and skull fracture. Discussion of the sun glare theory and the reported last words.

segments.title: Salvage and the cursed parts
segments.summary: The wrecked car was sent to a salvage yard. William Eschrich bought it, took the engine for his race car and gave the transmission and suspension to Troy Lee McHenry. Both later crashed in the same 1956 Pomona race, killing McHenry, which fueled the curse idea. McHenry's widow then gave his parts to other racers.

segments.title: George Barris and the car's disappearance
segments.summary: George Barris claimed he bought the frame and body from Dean's family, sold tires, and lent the frame to the LA National Safety Council for a traveling warning display. The display reportedly fell and injured people and killed a truck driver. The car later reportedly caught fire in storage around 1960 and then vanished, while Barris kept claiming to have the chassis.

segments.title: Volo Auto Museum hidden-car tip
segments.summary: In 2015 a man told Volo Auto Museum director Brian Grahams he had seen his father and friends hide the car in a false wall as a child. The man passed a polygraph, but the building had been demolished, so the car was not recovered.

segments.title: Transaxle auction
segments.summary: A transaxle believed to be from the car, which came from McHenry's widow, sold at auction in March 2020 for almost $400,000, reportedly to Zak Bagans. The hosts find the price surprising.

segments.title: Sign-off and Smokey and the Bandit door tangent
segments.summary: Hosts joke about making a coffee table from the Smokey and the Bandit sheriff's car door that Chuck's dad had kept in the garage, then sign off.
